citations.quote: Vuk Đukić
Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic

Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

plan.question: Joint project topic: Can autoencoder reconstruction error thresholds be adapted to detect anomalies across both Modbus and BACnet protocols on resource-constrained embedded hardware without labelled attack data? Conditional industrial PhD topic (post-pilot): How can multi-protocol temporal sliding windows and quantization techniques optimize on-device neural reconstruction for zero-day industrial control network threat detection?
plan.experiment: Proposed 12-week bench test: Train autoencoder models on ArmaturaSec's multi-terabyte benign traffic captures (Modbus and BACnet). Evaluate anomaly scoring using reconstruction thresholds on testbed-injected function code, coil manipulation, and replay anomaly scenarios executed on the company's hardware bench.
plan.metrics: Baseline: Supervised classifier baseline which produced unacceptable false positive rates on unlabelled deployments. Go/No-Go decision threshold: Achieve >90% anomaly detection across synthetic injection tests while maintaining a false positive rate <2% and execution latency <50ms per traffic window on ProtoSense hardware bench.
plan.companyAsk: ArmaturaSec role: Provide access to 1-2 part-time engineers, anonymized client traffic archives, hardware bench, and firmware codebase under NDA.
plan.researcherAsk: Researcher role: Provide autoencoder network architectures, encoding granularity parameters, and statistical reconstruction thresholding algorithms for protocol anomaly scoring.
plan.milestones: Weeks 1-4: Data ingestion and protocol windowing definition; Deliverable D1: Preprocessed traffic baseline set. Weeks 5-8: Model training and on-device inference optimization; Deliverable D2: Bench-deployed autoencoder model. Weeks 9-12: Synthetic injection validation and false positive benchmark; Deliverable D3: Pilot evaluation report.
plan.risks: Unknowns include computational overhead of BACnet parsing on edge hardware, sensitivity to multi-protocol traffic drift, and potential latency spikes during window reconstruction.
plan.meeting: First-week actions: ArmaturaSec lead prepares traffic archive samples under NDA; Researcher supplies reference autoencoder specifications. Kickoff agenda: Review NDA terms, establish data format conventions, and schedule weekly technical syncs.

As stated in the challenge description, "Three of our last five PCB designs failed radiated emissions at a third-party EMC lab on the first submission, typically between 150–450 MHz, which costs us on average €9,000 per re-test visit and delays client projects by six to ten weeks; we need a systematic way to predict and fix emission hotspots during layout review rather than after the fact." To support this experimental research, company C025 provides concrete engineering capacity: "We can allocate one senior hardware engineer and one firmware engineer part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our lab equipment and internal board archives under NDA." value.interpretation: To address Nexara Embedded d.o.o.'s challenge of identifying radiated emission hotspots during PCB layout review prior to third-party lab testing, Dijana Radulović (R0637) provides a relevant technical mechanism through automated layout scoring. In SYN-PUB-07261, titled 'Automated PCB Layout Scoring for EMC Risk Using Feature Extraction and a Rule-Based Engine', she developed a rule-based tool that ingests Gerber files and netlists to extract geometric features related to EMC risk—such as trace-to-plane spacing, edge distance, and decoupling capacitor placement—and flags potential violations automatically. If integrated into Nexara's pre-sign-off review, this rule-checking workflow could hypothetically serve as an early design gate to catch layout defects before laboratory submission. Dr. Radulović's stated collaboration interests include contract research on PCB EMC characterisation, consulting on EMC design review strategies, and joint projects combining simulation with industrial prototype testing. Her notes indicate an interest in longer-term collaborative projects involving real hardware from industrial partners, as well as potential access to her near-field scanning bench on a cost-recovery basis.

citations.quote: Dijana Radulović
Automated PCB Layout Scoring for EMC Risk Using Feature Extraction and a Rule-Based Engine

Manual EMC design review is time-consuming and relies on reviewer expertise that varies across organisations. This paper describes a rule-based layout scoring tool that ingests Gerber files and a netlist, extracts geometric features related to emission risk, and outputs a numerical score and flagged violation list. Seventeen rules were derived from simulation studies and published guidelines, covering trace-to-plane spacing, clock trace routing distance from board edge, decoupling capacitor placement relative to device power pins, and via stub length. The tool was implemented in Python using open-source Gerber parsing libraries. Validation was performed by scoring 23 PCB designs of known emission performance; boards that failed CISPR 22 Class B measurements scored below the threshold in 19 out of 23 cases (83% sensitivity). False-positive rate was 22%. Run time for a 20-layer board with 4000 components averaged 38 seconds. The tool is intended as an early design gate rather than a replacement for simulation or pre-compliance measurement.

citations.quote: Jelena Marković
industrial PhD supervision; joint projects
Packaging material permeability screening for MAP of mixed-berry trays

Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.
